full_judgment:
3. Defendant-1 Appellant contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to Nabin Chandra Mondal and that he took settlement of .69 decimals of land at a jama of Tk. 2/1/6 pies in 1334 B.S., thereafter took settlement of 1.00 acre at a jama of Tk. 3/- in 1336 B.S. and that he has since been possessing the land. The rent receiving interest of the Touji was subsequently auction purchased by Jarafat Munshi end Sara Begum and thereafter he paid rent to the new landlords at an amalgamated jama of Tk. 5/1/6 pies. The plaintiff has no title and possession in the suit land who taking advantage of the wrong record during S.A. operation filed this suit with a view to grab the suit property. 

 5. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the findings of fact arrived at by the lower appellate court on consideration of evidence have been illegally disturbed by the learned Judge of the High Court Division on misconstruction of documentary evidence, particularly the rent-receipts produced by the parties and also on wrong view of law taken by the learned Single Judge, in respect of the proceeding under section 19(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 7. In the instant case the learned Subordinate Judge proceeded to consider the respective cases of the plaintiff and defendant upon reiterating the age-old axiom that the plaintiff must succeed on his own case and weakness of defendant's case is no ground for passing a decree in favour of the plaintiff. The Subordinate Judge after finding that the plaintiff's case has not been proved went on to hold further that be agreed with the trial court that the story of lease set up by the defendant was unacceptable and that the defendant's title also was not proved. It seems that the learned Judge of High Court Division failed to appreciate the approach and findings made by the Sub-ordinate Judge, for, it will be seen that quite a large part of the impugned judgment is devoted to the consideration of the defendant's weakness (as to his dakhilas, rejection of objection under section 19(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act) which was wholly unnecessary as the same did not prove or strengthen the plaintiff's case. The learned Judge found fault with the subordinate judge for not considering the weakness of the defendant's case and particularly the rent receipts produced by him and  thus considered himself justified to interfere in second appeal. It must be said that the learned Judge made a fundamental mistake in ignoring altogether that the defendant's case was disbelieved by the lower appellate court but even then the plaintiff was held not to be entitled to a decree as he could not establish his own case. 

 8. As regards plaintiff’s case of title to the suit land it is based on the kabala (Ext. 2) dated 11.12.56 executed on behalf of Radha Prasanna and others. In the original plaint nothing was said as to how Radha Prasanna and others acquired title to the suit-land. Defendant-appellant in this written statement filed more than a year after the institution of the suit on 31.5.74 stated that he took settlement of the suit land in 1334 and 1336 B.S. from the C.S. recorded tenant Nabin Chandra Mondal, Plaintiff then, it seems, became wiser and amended his plaint about one year after the filing of the written statement introducing case for the first time that his vendors also took settlement of the suit land from Nabin Chandra in 1319 B.S. He filed the alleged pattani dakhilas on 19.9.76 long after filing of the written statement by the defendant. This aspect of the case whether Radha Prasanna took settlement from Nabin Chandra became of crucial importance in view of the plaintiff's omission to mention about the said fact in the original plaint and failure to file the Pattani dakhilas at the time of the institution of the suit although the plaintiff admitted in his evidence that they knew about Radha Parasanna's settlement from Nabin Chandra at the time of exchange and they had obtained the Pattani dakhilas at that time. The learned Subordinate Judge viewed the belated amendment of the plaint with shrewd suspicion and upon an intelligent analysis of the evidence and circumstances came to the conclusion that the plaintiff's case as to settlement by Nabin Chandra with Radha Prasanna had not been proved. It is unfortunate that the learned Judge of the High Court Division failed to notice the import of the Subordinate Judge's appreciation of the circumstances of the case relating to belated amendment of the plaint which cast a doubt on the plaintiff's case. The learned judge, it appears, quite unnecessarily took upon himself the task of explaining the law at length as to amendment of plaint which was never in doubt. It is, however, strange that it did not occur to him that the subsequent amendment of the plaint seeking to clothe Radha Prasanna with a title in the circumstances of the case raised genuine doubt as to plaintiff's case. Not only the amendment was belated but the alleged Pattani Dakhilas which were the only proof of Radha Prasanna's alleged settlement and were allegedly with the plaintiff from the time of exchange were produced long after the institution of the suit. There was no other evidence to prove alleged settlement with Radha Prasanna except the two doubtful Dakhilas Ext. 1 (kha) and 1 (ga). The Subordinate Judge noticed that the plaintiff did not even examine Sarafat Munshi who was alive and to whom rent was allegedly paid and Dakhilas Ext. 1 and 1 (ka) were obtained. The learned Judge of the High Court Division ignoring the consideration which weighed with the Subordinate Judge to discard the plaintiff's dakhilas proceeded to consider the defendant's dakhilas unnecessarily forgetting that both the courts below disbelieved the defendant's case. How misdirected was the learned Judge will be seen from the Judgment, to quote his own words, "this (defendant's dakhila) had not been considered by the court of appeal below and this being a basic document of title sought to be used by the defendant a finding arrived at by a non consideration and misconstruction or misreading of the said document would amount to a question of law which need to be interfered with by this court in its appellate jurisdiction". It must be said that the learned Judge made an entirely wrong approach to the case and the impugned judgment before him and failed to notice that there was neither any error of law or procedure in the judgment of the Sub-ordinate Judge calling for interference with the finding of fact arrived at by him. If Radha Prasanna's settlement was not proved as found by the Subordinate Judge, the plaintiff could not derive any title from kabala Ext. 2, no matter whether the Power of Attorney was genuine or not.
